title: Objection and reply
description: The objection, the strongest Christian reply, and the response, side by side. Filled with the 5:47 objection; replace the three paragraphs for a new one.
content: The Qur’an tells the People of the Injīl to judge by what God sent down in it (5:47). A book no one could read would be no standard to judge by, so the Injīl the Qur’an affirms must be the gospels Christians held.

Seventh-century Christians possessed the four gospels, in Greek and Syriac, and nothing else under the name of gospel. The Qur’an speaks of the Injīl “with them” (7:157). Therefore it endorses the gospels in their hands (Gordon Nickel, The Gentle Answer, 2015; Samuel Green, “The Gospel in the Qur’an”).

The verse commands judgement by what God revealed in the Injīl, and the verse before it says the Injīl was given to ʿĪsā (5:46). The books Christians held carried that revelation and other matter besides, which is why the same Qur’an both appeals to them (7:157) and corrects them (2:79; 5:13-14). Possession of a book is not the identity of a revelation. See The Islamic Dilemma, answered.
